newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's August C/A deficit widens to $3.49 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's August C/A deficit widens to $3.49 bln.

text.p: South Korea's current account deficit expanded to $3.49 billion in August from a $828.3 million shortfall a year earlier, preliminary figures from the Bank of Korea showed on Tuesday.
NOTE - Figures are in millions of US dollars.
The August deficit compared with a shortfall of $2.28 billion in July.
The deficit for the first eight months of this year amounted to $15.24 billion, sharply up from a $7.33 billion shortfall a year earlier.
The eight-month shortfall was more than double the government's original target of a $7 billion deficit for the whole of this year.
Both the trade and invisible trade deficit continued to grow, due mainly to sluggish exports and increased tourist spending abroad.
The trade deficit for the eight-month period rose to $9.72 billion from a $4.81 billion shortfall a year earlier.
Exports of chemical and heavy-industrial products fell 13.5 percent to $6.48 billion in August from $7.49 billion in the same month of 1995, the statement said.
Electronics goods, including semiconductors, led the decline in exports of heavy-industrial goods by falling 25.3 percent year-on-year to $1.78 billion in August.
Imports maintained a steady pace, rising 12.4 percent year-on-year to $12.94 billion in August.
